what_it_does: This paper presents a specialized chip for voice-activated devices like smart home speakers or fitness trackers that listen all the time but use almost no power. The challenge is handling human speech that varies wildly in volume—from a whisper to shouting—while still understanding complete sentences (not just recognizing single words). The design combines automatic volume control circuitry at the input stage with an artificial neural network that processes speech as a stream and skips unnecessary computation when audio is quiet, keeping power consumption below 9 microwatts.
